content:
ESPN analyst Jesse Palmer caught a young couple apparently quarreling in the stands of Georgia Tech’s game against Wake Forest in Atlanta ― and he seized the moment for the TV audience.

The former New York Giants quarterback, who later became a “Bachelor” lead, now hosts the ABC dating program. So he went with his training and narrated what he thought was going on between the two fans.

Tech was getting slaughtered by Wake on Saturday in an eventual 50-29 defeat, so the impromptu departure was perhaps welcomed.

“This playoff situation is intense right now; maybe not as intense as this conversation, though,” Palmer said as the camera focused on the pair.

Egged on by play-by-play partner Joe Tessitore to “break it down,” Palmer said: “He is locked in. He is holding her to court right now. He wants an answer and he’s not leaving. They are in each other’s personal space. He’s not happy with whatever she just told him. ... This is kind of one of those moments where you just say ‘I’m sorry.’ Please take a moment and say your goodbyes.’”

But if there was tension, it seemed that the college football Romeo made up with his Juliet. They were later seen kissing on the broadcast.

“Embrace the love, America,” Tessitore said.

“OK, get a room, though,” Palmer chimed in.

There was no rose extended, but it did seem to be a somewhat happy ending.

As the lead on “The Bachelor,” Palmer gave out the show’s coveted final rose without a proposal, and the relationship later fizzled. He was named the new host in 2021 and also hosts other shows in the “Bachelor” universe.

Palmer reportedly persuaded current NFL quarterback Sam Hartman, who was hesitant to star in the reality show, to become the next “Bachelor” lead.

The host already seems to be in midseason form for the new season’s taping next year.
